The VaQuitA paper presents a well-motivated, coherently designed framework for zero-shot video question answering that combines data-level and feature-level alignment. Its key strengths are the systematic two-level alignment approach, parameter-efficient design (only training lightweight modules while freezing the encoder and LLM), and consistent SOTA-level results across three benchmarks. The performance gains are cleanly ablated and meaningful.

However, the weaknesses are material: (1) multi-turn conversation claims are entirely unsupported (anecdotal examples only), which undermines the paper's broader claims of industrial applicability; (2) several baseline comparisons are uncontrolled, with the massive (17.4%) jump on MSRVTT-QA raising suspicion of pipeline differences rather than genuine model superiority; (3) the core design difference of inverted Q/K/V is not ablated against a standard configuration, so its claimed necessity is unproven; (4) the test-time effectiveness of the data alignment module is unsupported; (5) the prompt "Please be critical" improvements are tiny and overstated. There are no fatal flaws, but the accumulation of these moderate issues is significant.

Comparing to anchors: 
- This paper is clearly stronger than the rejected ones (e.g., Harry Potter, Score 1-3; Projected Subnetworks, Score 1-3). 
- It is comparable to or slightly stronger than papers that were borderline accept (e.g., Video Q-Former, Scores 3-5; Valley, Scores 3-6) because it has better ablation rigor and overall architecture coherence. 
- It is notably weaker than clearly accepted papers like Representation Alignment (Scores 8-10) or TANGO (Scores 8-10), which have transformative concepts or thorough validation of their claims. 
- The Video-STaR paper (Scores 5-8) had systematic limitations in baselines but introduced a novel self-training paradigm; VaQuitA has a weaker novelty claim but stronger architectural motivation. Overall, VaQuitA sits at the borderline accept to reject boundary.
